messages:
maya: quick check — need permission to pull a handful of raw llm traces for a privacy audit. only 5 trace ids, will redact before sharing. how narrow can we scope this?
jonathan: can you paste the trace ids + which project they live in? also who needs access?
maya: project = redwood-llm-prod, ids = trace-2026-03-15-01, trace-2026-03-15-02, trace-2026-03-15-09, trace-2026-03-15-22, trace-2026-03-16-03. requestor = external auditor (Gabrielle), internal reviewer = me.
sam: ok two things: 1) prefer a short-lived binding to a least-priv svcacct instead of handing org-level role to gabrielle. 2) ensure log redaction (user ids + emails) before any export.
gabrielle: i can use ephemeral access. i'd like read-only access to logs & llm-traces (no KMS, no dataset export). can we do a view-only role with a filter?
maya: ideal flow: create a tenant-scoped service account, grant roles/logging.viewer on project:redwood-llm-prod, bind only to a filter that matches those trace ids, then issue a 2-hour signed token to gabrielle. after 2h revoke.
jonathan: security question: does roles/logging.viewer allow access to raw payload that could contain PII? if so we need to run a redact job first or restrict fields.
audit-bot: policy-snippet: "For sensitive traces containing user identifiers, require 'trace:read' with field-level redaction or use Data Loss Prevention (DLP) pipeline prior to export."
sam: +1 to DLP. practical approach: grant viewer, but block export/exportToStorage via IAM condition. then run a redact lambda that strips keys 'user_id', 'email', 'session_token' and write to a temp GCS bucket with restricted perms.
gabrielle: that works for me. i just need console/log view and the ability to peek at the full event payload in console for debugging; redact job should run first though.
maya: can someone post the minimal IAM binding snippet i should apply?
sam: use this (apply with least privilege):
```
resource: //cloudresourcemanager.googleapis.com/projects/redwood-llm-prod
role: roles/logging.viewer
member: serviceAccount:auditor-jit@redwood-infra.iam.gserviceaccount.com
condition:
  title: "trace-id-filter"
  expression: "resource.labels.project_id == 'redwood-llm-prod' && (jsonPayload.traceId == 'trace-2026-03-15-01' || jsonPayload.traceId == 'trace-2026-03-15-02' || jsonPayload.traceId == 'trace-2026-03-15-09' || jsonPayload.traceId == 'trace-2026-03-15-22' || jsonPayload.traceId == 'trace-2026-03-16-03')"
  description: "limit to listed traces"
duration: "7200s"  # 2 hours via short-lived token
```
jonathan: quick note — IAM conditions on logging might not support jsonPayload.traceId on all backends. if that fails, use a temporary BigQuery export of matching traces + DLP job. but try condition first.
maya: thanks. i'll try the conditional binding and the redact lambda. i'll tag you both when i spin up the temp SA and token.
sam: please add a ticket linking the export bucket + redact job and set retention=1d for that bucket. also audit log that the SA was used.
gabrielle: thanks all, will wait for the redacted dump. :thumbsup:
maya: done — created ticket RW-4521, created SA auditor-jit@redwood-infra.iam.gserviceaccount.com, applying conditional viewer now, will post token once DLP run completes.
jonathan: approved for 2h window, confirm when token issued and when bucket has redact logs.
maya: will close thread when everything done.
